title: What is DevOps for Data Engineering?

scenes.heading: What is DevOps for Data Engineering?
scenes.narration: DevOps for data engineering brings software delivery discipline to the world of pipelines, warehouses, and analytics.

scenes.heading: The core ideas
bullets: Version control for code, config, and infrastructure
Collaboration between data, platform, and ops teams
scenes.narration: Automation replaces fragile manual steps so that deployments become repeatable and predictable. Version control tracks not just application code but also configuration and infrastructure definitions. Continuous integration gives you fast feedback when a change breaks something. Finally, collaboration tears down the wall between the people who build pipelines and the people who run them.

scenes.heading: From commit to production
scenes.narration: A change begins as code and tests written by an engineer and committed to a shared repository. Continuous integration then builds and validates that change automatically. Once it passes, it is deployed and continuously monitored, and the observations feed back into the next iteration.

scenes.heading: Traditional vs DevOps way
scenes.narration: In the traditional approach, deployments are manual and configuration hides on individual machines, which makes releases slow and risky. The DevOps approach automates the pipeline and stores everything in version control, enabling releases that are both frequent and safe.

scenes.text: DevOps for data engineering is a culture plus a toolchain: automate, version, test, and monitor so your pipelines ship reliably.
scenes.narration: The essential lesson is that DevOps combines a collaborative culture with an automated toolchain so your data pipelines ship reliably and repeatably.
